categories.main_business_segments: Chori Co., Ltd. operates three main business segments: the Textile Business, which handles synthetic and natural fiber raw materials, textiles, apparel, and industrial textile materials; the Chemicals Business, which deals with urethane materials, resins, additives, glass materials, electronic materials, pharmaceuticals, and food/feed additives; and the Machinery Business, which focuses on vehicles and related equipment. The company also has a minor segment for other services such as administrative outsourcing.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Chori's core capabilities lie in its global trading, supply chain management, and value-added distribution of textiles, chemicals, and machinery. The company emphasizes high-functionality and specialty materials, sustainable and circular textile schemes (e.g., B-LOOP® for textile-to-textile recycling), and advanced IT/DX systems for operational efficiency. Manufacturing is generally outsourced, with Chori acting as a value-adding intermediary and developer of new business models.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Chori serves a wide range of B2B customers, including manufacturers in the apparel, automotive, electronics, chemical, and industrial sectors. Its end markets are diverse, spanning clothing and fashion, industrial materials, electronics, automotive, healthcare, and food/feed industries. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of sales, indicating a broad and diversified client base.
categories.geographic_coverage: Chori operates globally, with major business activities in Japan, China, and other Asian countries, as well as North America and Europe. China is a particularly important market and production base, but the company also maintains significant operations and subsidiaries in Southeast Asia, the US, and Europe. Sales are well-diversified geographically, with Japan, China, and other regions each contributing substantial portions of revenue.
categories.supply_chain_position: Chori primarily operates as a midstream trading company (sogo shosha), acting as an intermediary between upstream raw material producers and downstream manufacturers or end-users. The company adds value through logistics, procurement, product development, and supply chain optimization, often coordinating between suppliers and customers across borders.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Chori's strategic focus is on sustainable growth through high-functionality, specialty products, and global business expansion. Key initiatives include strengthening global business operations, expanding sustainable and circular business models (notably in textiles), promoting ESG management, and accelerating digital transformation (DX) through company-wide IT system upgrades. R&D spending is modest and mainly directed at textile materials and new chemical applications, with a strong emphasis on market-driven innovation and environmental solutions.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of goods as a trading company, purchasing products from suppliers and selling them to customers. Revenue is recognized at the point of delivery or shipment. Chori also earns income from logistics, administrative services, and, to a lesser extent, licensing and investment activities.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Chori is positioned as a specialized trading company with strengths in textiles and chemicals, operating under the umbrella of Toray Industries (its parent company). Major competitors include other Japanese sogo shosha (general trading companies) and specialized trading firms in textiles and chemicals. Chori differentiates itself through its focus on high-functionality, sustainability, and global supply chain integration, and is considered a leading player in its niche markets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, Chori reported consolidated net sales of ¥311.5 billion, operating income of ¥14.5 billion, and net income attributable to shareholders of ¥11.7 billion, with total assets of ¥146.1 billion and equity of ¥92.1 billion. The company has demonstrated steady growth, achieving record profits for four consecutive years, and targets further expansion with a mid-term plan aiming for ¥330 billion in sales and ¥16 billion in pre-tax profit for FY2026.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Chori emphasizes its ability to deliver high-value, high-functionality, and specialty products with a strong focus on sustainability and customer satisfaction. Its unique value proposition lies in its global network, expertise in supply chain management, and ability to develop and deliver innovative, environmentally responsible solutions tailored to customer needs. The company also highlights its commitment to ESG, digital transformation, and the creation of sustainable business models as key differentiators.
